prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms, which brought frequency metrology to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for optical lattice clocks to Katori and Ye. In answer to the chair's first question, what the citation recognises that the 2005 and 2012 prizes did not is the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice: many atoms held with the clock transition's light shift cancelled, which turned a single-ion or free-atom measurement into a many-atom one and made 10^-18 accuracy and stability reachable. The comb made optical frequencies countable and ion control gave single-particle clocks; the lattice is a separate concept, not the same tool refined. On the second question, two names are defensible because the concept and first demonstration sit with Katori and the push to the accuracy and stability frontier with Ye; Takamoto, Lemonde, Ludlow and Derevianko made real contributions but none displaces either name without breaking the concept-plus-realisation logic. I would not wait for the redefinition of the second: the performance is independently reproduced in several national laboratories and the interpretation is stable. The round-1 exchange strengthened my view that this is the only configuration where science, maturity and attribution all hold without a trade-off, and the other supporters have written the same citation basis, which I adopt.
statement.case_against: The residual weakness is still cumulative recognition. Johansson, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce all concede, as I do, that a sceptic can read the clocks as the next step in a line honoured in 2005 and 2012, and Danielsson and Mehlig weigh that more heavily than I do. The citation must therefore be tied to the lattice concept and not to metrology in general, or it will read as a prize for precision. Second, the redefinition of the second has not happened, so the largest practical payoff is prospective. Third, the omission of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and others from a two-name credit is a judgement the committee should make openly, not a settled fact.

responses.point: Mehlig accepts that B002 wins on attribution and maturity but judges the discovery content of twisted bilayer graphene to be larger because it opened a new regime of correlated matter, and he would not oppose B002 if maturity is weighted more heavily.
responses.response: I think that is the real disagreement and it is a fair one. I do not read the statutes as asking which field is larger; they ask for a discovery or invention of the greatest importance, and a new regime of what can be measured, with fundamental-constant tests and geodesy already following from it, meets that. Your own conditions are what keep me from moving. You say the pairing mechanism is unsettled, that the citation must be worded around the platform and not an explanation, and that experimental credit is shared with Cao and others outside three names. I would be comfortable with B038 in a few years, once those points have settled; I do not think the committee has to pick the larger field when a smaller but finished achievement is ready.

responses.point: Eriksson says B002 is the most mature and cleanly attributed candidate but a refinement of an established programme, and that he could accept it as the second part of a two-part prize.
responses.response: I note that offer, and the chair asked about pairs. I would not support B002 plus B038 this year. The two parts rest on different grounds: one is mature and attributed, the other is a prediction and discovery whose mechanism the field has not resolved, and putting them together would not repair B038's maturity problem, it would borrow B002's. What would change my mind on B038 is independent identification of the pairing mechanism, or at least a settled consensus on the nature of the correlated phases, together with a defensible credit rule for the experimental side. Absent that, I keep B038 as my first alternative because the theory-plus-experiment story is the cleanest in condensed matter.

responses.point: Danielsson says the 2005 and 2012 prizes make B002 look like the next step in precision metrology, and he keeps B053 first while saying he would meet the attribution problem by tying the citation to conception and leadership of the experiments.
responses.response: I now list B053 as an alternative, because I accept the science is exceptional and the experimental side was left unrecognised in 2013. I still cannot support it first. Tying the citation to conception and leadership is a rule, but it rewards institutional leadership and not the delivery of the 2012 analyses, and the chair's question about a principled rule stays open in your statement. If you can show a rule that a collaboration member would accept as fair, I would reconsider, but I would want it stated in the citation itself. On novelty, I see the lattice as a distinct concept, not a repeat of the comb or ion control.

responses.point: Lindroth is less comfortable with B033 than our shared second place suggests because Wineland and Monroe are central to the experimental credit and the 2012 and 2022 prizes cover neighbouring material.
responses.response: I agree and I have dropped B033 from my alternatives. The experimental credit is split across several ion-trap laboratories, the first-gate work sits beneath the 2012 prize, and the 2022 prize touches the same foundations, so the novelty margin is thinner than for the clocks. I replace it with B053, on science and maturity, while saying openly that it has the attribution problem we both described. This also answers the earlier point that our shared choices are one view held twice, since my alternatives now differ from yours.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the lattice concept as distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system work, or reads the clocks as cumulative.
Whether the unreached redefinition of the second should lead the committee to wait; I treat 10^-18 performance as sufficient but others differ.

How the committee wants to divide credit between the lattice proposal and the long JILA programme, and whether Takamoto, Lemonde or Derevianko should join the two names. I have not verified detailed priority beyond my recollection.
Whether a principled credit rule for B053 exists that would make it competitive.
How the committee will handle my perceived connection to Jun Ye on the final ballot.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure: my profile documents a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and Jun Ye is associated with Hall's group and JILA, so I record a perceived connection to B002. The chair asked whether I should abstain. I leave that to the committee, though I note that it is a documented stay from long ago, I have no documented collaboration with Ye or Katori, and my own work in rare-earth-ion crystals and quantum memories does not overlap with lattice clocks. If the committee prefers that I abstain on B002, the other four first preferences remain. I record no tie to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Della Negra, Jenni or Virdee, and none of my listed Lund colleagues is credited on any shortlisted part.
